answer: For durable order-event delivery. The 2026-09-10 platform sync chose a transactional outbox because Redis pub/sub has durability problems — messages are lost on subscriber disconnect and there is no publisher-side acknowledgment; a postmortem (scope: order-event-delivery) measured ~0.4% order-event loss in a staging soak test, so Redis pub/sub was rejected where at-least-once delivery is required. The transcript explains the mechanism: events are written in the same Postgres transaction as the order state change, then relayed.
effort_notes: rg -n -i outbox (1 search, 6 hits across 5 files); read notes/meeting-2026-09-10.md, notes/failed-redis-pubsub.md, transcripts/session-2026-09-12.md (3 reads).
